title: Prevalence and Characteristics of Gastrointestinal Symptoms in Pediatric Palliative Care Patients – A Retrospective Cohort Analysis Over 10 Years
summary:
Children and adolescents with severe life-limiting illnesses often suffer from stomach and bowel problems as well as difficulties with nutrition and feeding. These may include nausea, vomiting, constipation, diarrhea, abdominal pain, or problems with eating and drinking. So far, only limited research has investigated how common these problems are in children receiving palliative care.

This study will analyze the medical records of all patients treated on the pediatric palliative care ward at LMU University Hospital Munich between 2016 and 2026. The study will examine which symptoms occur most frequently, which types of nutrition are used, and how often changes in nutritional support were necessary. In addition, available laboratory results and severe clinical complications will be evaluated.

The aim of the study is to improve future care for children and adolescents with severe illnesses and to better adapt treatment to their individual needs.
conditions: The diagnoses of the pediatric palliative care patients included in the study were classified according to the ICD-10 classification and the categories defined by Together for Short Lives (TfSL).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients who received inpatient treatment on the pediatric palliative care ward between 06/2016 and 05/2026 and for whom routine clinical data, including laboratory results, were available in the electronic medical records.
No fixed age limit was defined, as in individual cases patients continued to receive follow-up care after reaching adulthood within the framework of ongoing care. Age will be documented as a variable and taken into account in the analysis.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who were admitted only for short-term inpatient care (e.g. postoperative monitoring, transfusions, intravenous iron substitution, bisphosphonate administration, or MRI examinations).
